- When sentiment is bullish (≥0.67) and model shows gradual upward trend, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model tends to overshoot; cap forecast growth to +3–4% per day unless sentiment remains strong.
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model overestimates upside; apply downward bias of 1–2% to forecast mean.
- When multiple auction events occur in short window (e.g., 3+ auctions/30d), model overreacts to supply shocks; reduce forecast volatility by 15–20%.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral), model tends to drift upward; apply mean reversion to forecast, pulling toward 10–15 day moving average.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from model, check if sentiment or supply events triggered a policy shift — if yes, adjust forecast to reflect new equilibrium.
